T1.title: Network fabric
T1.line: A slow answer is usually a request waiting in line, not a slow model, so teams measure the wait first.

T2.title: Retrieval
T2.line: Most wrong answers start here: if search misses the right note, no model can quote it.

T3.title: To the GPU server
T3.line: GPU time is the biggest cost, so the cheapest request is one that never needs a GPU.

acts.title: To the GPU server
acts.line: GPU time is the biggest cost, so the cheapest request is one that never needs a GPU.

acts.title: The drop
acts.line: One GPU server answers many people at once by batching their requests together.

acts.title: The descent
acts.line: Power and cooling, not chips alone, now limit how many GPUs a building can run.

T4.title: Prefill
T4.line: Reading the prompt is fast, but a long prompt is paid for on every request, so teams trim it.

T5.title: Decode
T5.line: Answers are written one piece at a time, so the answer's length decides most of the wait.

T6.title: KV cache
T6.line: Memory, not speed, caps how many chats one GPU can hold, and fixed-size blocks let it hold more.

T7.title: Eight GPUs
T7.line: A model too big for one chip is split across several, so the links between chips matter as much as the chips.

T8.title: Memory tiers
T8.line: Fast memory is small and costly, so good systems keep what is needed now close and move the rest out.

T9.title: The way out
T9.line: People remember the slowest answers, so teams watch the worst one in twenty, not the average.
